prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: deployable portfolio website concept screenshot
Primary request: Create a polished desktop website mockup for a game developer portfolio with a meaningful chatbot experience. This is concept 4 of 5 and should use a terminal-like explainer overlay layered over a clean portfolio.
Scene/backdrop: full-browser website screenshot, realistic high-fidelity web UI
Subject: clean portfolio homepage with structured sections for featured games, profile, and technology. Over part of the page sits a refined terminal-style assistant overlay that answers questions about the developer's architecture decisions, project roles, and strengths, with highlighted references back into the page.
Style/medium: elegant technical product UI, not hacker parody, practical and shippable
Composition/framing: dominant clean page grid underneath, assistant overlay floating near lower left or center with highlighted anchors pointing to portfolio sections; visible game cards and skill blocks remain readable
Lighting/mood: precise, focused, analytical
Color palette: off-white, midnight navy, muted cyan, steel gray, restrained coral accents
Materials/textures: matte surfaces, crisp borders, subtle spotlighting behind overlay
Text (verbatim): "Projects", "Experience", "Tech", "Chatbot", "Ask", "Why this matters"
Constraints: terminal-like assistant should feel useful and credible, not gimmicky; clearly imply cross-linking between answer snippets and portfolio evidence; include sections for games, developer profile, technology, and chatbot; no watermark
Avoid: full dark-mode cyberpunk, retro green-screen cliché, clutter, collage
summary: Concept 04 keeps a conventional portfolio underneath but adds a technical explainer overlay that suggests evidence-backed Q&A for recruiters who want architecture and implementation detail fast.
generation_notes: Generated with the built-in image_gen tool in default mode. Included to cover the most technical chatbot entry pattern in Set B without turning the whole page into a gimmick terminal.
